newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mostly lower, feeders lower. [CORRECTED 19:42 GMT]
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mostly lower, feeders lower. [CORRECTED 19:42 GMT]

text.p: CME live cattle futures weakened again in the last few minutes of trade to offset midday short covering and end mostly lower, traders said. Feeder cattle also eased back again into the close.
Futures had drifted up from early lows linked to Friday's bearish USDA Cattle-on-Feed Report in light dealings, but fell again as late commercial selling met little resistance, traders said.
October had found support on expectations of continued firm live markets. Spreading of long February/short December influenced those months.

December showed the most pressure through the day from the cattle report. Cattle that were placed during August were at heavier weights and will be ready sooner than earlier expected, traders and analysts said.

The report showed August feedlot placements in the seven major feedlot states at 119 percent of a year ago -- the high end of early expectations. Marketings were at the low end of estimates at 91 percent and the number of cattle on feed as of September 1 was 92 percent of a year ago, the high end of estimates.
RBH bought October late but selling by R.J. O'Brien and a combination of profit taking and continued long liquidation near the close turned prices lower, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, Dean Witter bought February 68 calls, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle in thin trade, also falling late. But lower corn futures limited losses, traders said.
Prudential Securities and Cargill Investor Services sold into sell stops early. Stone Traders bought on the recovery and Cargill sold October again late, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.03 at $64.17 per cwt.

Live cattle closed 0.350 cent lower to 0.125 cent higher with October off most at 71.600 cents a lb. Feeder cattle ended 0.550 to 0.200 cent lower with October off most at 63.150 cents. (Corrects prices in final para from: Live cattle closed 0.250 cent lower to 0.275 cent higher with October off most at 0.025 at 71.925 cents a lb. Feeder cattle ended 0.100 to 0.325 lower with October off the least at 63.600 cents.)
